modality_summaries.modality: A — CI gates and exit-code plumbing
modality_summaries.summary:
Swept all 9 workflow files line by line, run_layer0.py in full (all 8 gates + --require/--require-fresh/--require-coverage + baseline interaction), scripts/ci_local.sh, .githooks/pre-push, scripts/check_downgrades.py, scripts/doctor.py orchestration, tests/test_ci_config.py (22 meta-tests) and tests/test_layer0_module_coverage.py as the anti-hollowing layer, plus live branch protection and the live secret/variable inventory via gh. Everything executed with .venv/bin/python; nothing mutated (only gitignored docs/assessment/_machine.json was regenerated by a repro).

Yield: 7 candidates, 5 with an executed repro, 4 of them in the path of a required check or the production deploy. The headline structural result is A1: the hardening primitive the project invented for this exact class (--require, Issue 479) is incapable BY CONSTRUCTION of catching how four of the eight Layer-0 gates actually fail — they report status "ok" with a perfect score of 0 when the underlying tool exits non-zero with empty stdout, and --require only rejects status "skipped". So the fix the process map recommends (add --require to static-gates) would not help. A3 is the same defect inside the ALREADY-hardened coverage job: gate_module_coverage returns "ok" when the five floor-gated modules are absent from coverage.xml, and the guard test written for Issue 368 checks that no floor VALUE is 0.0 rather than that any module's measured RATE resolves. A4 is the 10-week-Stripe-outage geometry still in place: deploy.yml's "Preflight check" runs doctor.py WITHOUT --full, so the gate on every prod deploy live-probes only Postgres and Redis — the corrected app-client-based Stripe/R2 probes run only when a human types --full by hand; and has_failures counts only Status.FAIL, so "cannot verify" (WARN) and "not configured" (SKIP) exit 0.

Also verified sound and recorded so nobody re-checks: migration-lint sets pipefail in both pipelines and its revision regex is safe against all 62 migrations (script.py.mako emits the un-annotated form); check_downgrades.py still runs its allowlist-staleness half with zero args; deploy.yml's alembic current==heads assertion fails closed; the render_env collect-count guard is real (measured exactly 7); the eval/clip-quality commit status targets PR head sha and fails closed; live branch protection matches docs/BRANCHING.md byte-for-byte today.

Off-class: gh secret/variable inventory confirms CC_JWT_SECRET, CC_CREATOR_ID, all four R2_*, SENTRY_DSN and both OTEL_* are unset — empirically confirming already-known findings #6 and #9, and showing deploy.yml's R2 secret sync (added after a prod upload silently failed) is a no-op on every deploy while the same step unconditionally pins STORAGE_BACKEND=r2.

Full analysis at docs/assessment/DEEP_AUDIT_2026-08-17/02-sweep/mA-gates-exitcodes.md

Swept 260 test modules / 3,068 test functions / 3,234 gating tests plus the 6 frontend structural gates, pattern-first via four AST sweeps (assertion shapes, parametrize sources, asserting-loops-over-dynamic-iterables, and a full census of module-level literals in tests/ + scripts/ + .claude/skills/.../run_layer0.py). Everything run with .venv/bin/python (fastapi 0.137.1) or the repo's own npx vitest / npx vite build.

Honest yield: the "always-true assertion" and "empty iteration" sweeps came back near-clean — exactly 1 `assert True` (deliberate, inside a self-test about the quarantine marker), 1 `except: pass` (deliberate service probe in conftest), and ZERO parametrize-over-empty. All dynamic parametrize sources are floor-guarded. That is a genuine, creditable result and I am reporting it as such rather than padding.

The entire yield is concentrated in ONE shape: the hand-maintained literal registry. I found 101 module-level list/tuple/set/dict literals in tests/ + scripts/, diffed the ~20 that define a gate's SCOPE against ground truth, and 11 had drifted. Three of those drifts are covering a defect that is live on main today:
 (1) the per-creator daily-quota gate iterates a 9-name literal while 17 routes carry the LLM flag — 4 of the 8 unchecked routes violate the invariant, including POST /creators/me/dna/build which has NO daily cap and a 120/minute burst on a Sonnet DNA build;
 (2) the design-token contract gate uses a 17-name denylist, and `bg-surface-raised` (x2) + `bg-accent-subtle` (x1) are live and verified ABSENT from the built CSS — the identical defect the gate was written from;
 (3) the RLS regression test still hardcodes its table tuple (the fix for a prior vacuous-green bug replaced a 2-item literal with a 17-item literal) while 26 tables carry a tenant_isolation policy — 8 policy-bearing tenant tables have never been exercised.

Every candidate carries a runnable repro; B1, B2, B3, B5 and B10 were measured live on this tree (route resolver + limiter._route_limits introspection, a vite build with a grep over the emitted CSS, a migration-wide policy scan, an instrumented OpenAPI crawl showing 29/34 responses are HTTP 401, and an APIRoute count of 6 of 126).

I also verified and am reporting as SOUND: test_usage_coverage's layer-2 billing sweep (real AST discovery, bidirectional map check — the model the others should copy), test_worker_invariants' allowlist contents, test_scoring_goldens' schema+model pins, test_principles_registry's 4-site map (correct today), frontend sourceScan.ts, and the eval anti-hollowing guards.

Full analysis at docs/assessment/DEEP_AUDIT_2026-08-17/02-sweep/mB-tests-that-cannot-fail.md, including an "Off-class" section with 3 items (two live cost-safety rate-limit gaps and two real-ffmpeg regression tests sitting in the soft-install lane).

Swept every artefact in the repo that ATTESTS a subsystem is alive: scripts/doctor.py line by line, live_smoke.py, llm_harness.py, drills.py, llm_e2e.py, check_downgrades.py, backup_pg.sh/backup_redis.sh, deploy.sh, ci_local.sh, r2_inspect.py, clip_audit.py; the /health endpoint plus compose healthchecks; deploy.yml (staging gate + prod smoke + rollback), staging-drills.yml, health-check.yml, llm-e2e-nightly.yml, ci.yml's migration-lint; and the meta-gates in tests/test_ci_config.py and tests/test_doctor.py. Method: for each probe, ask (a) does it reach the dependency by the path the app uses, (b) what exactly can be dead while it stays green, (c) is the success string emitted per-loop or per-kept-item, (d) is its fixture derived from what it checks. Yield: 9 candidates, 4 high, 2 with executed/exact repros. Full write-up at /home/reese/workspace/Youtube-Video-AI-Editor/docs/assessment/DEEP_AUDIT_2026-08-17/02-sweep/mC-probes-and-scripts.md. The organising finding: the project FIXED the canonical instance (_live_stripe now goes through billing.stripe_client._STRIPE, with 3 regression tests) but the fix lives behind `doctor.py --full`, and the automated deploy gate at deploy.yml:279 and deploy.sh:97 invokes doctor WITHOUT --full — so the entire "Live — external APIs" section (Anthropic, Voyage, Deepgram, R2, Stripe) has never run in any scheduled job. The same "the correct mechanism exists somewhere, but not on the path that actually runs" pattern repeats three more times: the alembic current==head assertion exists in staging + the manual fallback but not the prod job; the collect-only count guard exists for the render_env lane but not for the nightly live lanes; the app-client fix was applied to _live_r2 but the operation is still read-only. I also verified clean and say so explicitly: scripts/drills.py (the rate-limit drill's all([]) hole is genuinely closed by the first_429 == limit assertion), ci.yml's migration-lint (pipefail set at both dangerous pipes), tests/test_doctor.py's probe-integrity pins, and the backup scripts. Two things I could not verify from this repo and flagged with the exact settling command: whether the Cloudflare Health Check exists/is unsuspended/has the response-body match enabled, and whether the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / DEEPGRAM_API_KEY repository secrets are actually set (candidate mC-2 is vacuous only if they are not — the defect is that the repo cannot tell, and reports green either way).

Honest framing: the catalog-sync lesson WAS internalised where it was learned — youtube/data_api.py:294 separates seen from kept, youtube/analytics.py:299 counts inserts, worker/tasks.py:4899-4952 carries the postmortem comment verbatim and counts fetched vs attempted, ingestion/signals.py:100-112 is a model raw-vs-kept boundary. The three I would defend as the same class as the four the brief names: (1) NOTIFY_BACKEND defaults to "console" with no production validator, so every notification is committed status=sent and logged "email sent" over a code path whose own docstring says it never calls an external service — structurally identical to the STORAGE_BACKEND=local prod incident that DID earn a validator; doctor.py has zero Resend/email probes and deploy.yml does not sync the var. (3) Both post-deploy smoke phases exec inside the app container and /health has no Celery/queue component, so all three worker containers can crash-loop while up -d (no --wait), /health "ok", llm_harness "ALL REQUIRED STEPS PASSED" and the deploy job all report success — the compose file already defines correct `celery inspect ping` healthchecks that nothing in the pipeline or the monitor ever reads.

Also: clips_ready email/in-app fires unconditionally on 0 clips ("Your 0 clips ... are ready for review", repro'd), render_video_clips_done reports count=len(clip_ids) (attempted, not rendered) — the catalog-sync counter shape relocated to the default auto-render path, three Beat backfills increment `done` before the success check, the Issue-328 "why did I get N clips?" funnel breadcrumb is at DEBUG in a prod pinned to INFO where DEBUG is explicitly forbidden, an empty LLM score array degrades 100% of candidates to cold-start with zero log output, and generate_improvement_brief writes status=ready from zero analytics rows (its own comment records this failing once already under the RLS role split — the GUC was fixed, the unconditional `ready` was not).

modality_summaries.summary: Swept config.py (214 settings), .env.example, flags.py, scripts/doctor.py, deploy.yml, the three compose files, render.yaml, the Helm values, and every point where a third party is configured to call this app. Method: three read-only AST+grep scripts run under .venv/bin/python — (1) symmetric-diff Settings vs .env.example, (2) git grep -w every Settings field across the tree with config.py/.env.example/docs excluded, then hand-check the lowercase @property accessors, (3) find every off/empty-default setting and cross-check it against deploy.yml's secret sync, docker-compose.prod.yml, docker-compose.staging.yml, render.yaml and deploy/charts — followed by a manual pass over all nine externally-registered values. Full analysis at /home/reese/workspace/Youtube-Video-AI-Editor/docs/assessment/DEEP_AUDIT_2026-08-17/02-sweep/mE-config-flags-external.md. Honest yield: 11 candidates, 10 with a repro, 4 HIGH. The three I would defend as independent new instances of the class: (E1) the deploy step named "Preflight check" invokes scripts/doctor.py WITHOUT --full, so the five external-API probes — including the _live_stripe rewrite added on 2026-08-13 specifically to prevent recurrence of the 10-week outage — have never executed on any deploy; --full appears in zero workflows and zero scripts, only in eight prose files, and this also falsifies a factual claim at d08-deploy-observability.md:153. (E2) the staging-parity gate cannot exercise render or object storage at all: prod runs worker -Q celery plus render-worker -Q render, staging runs one worker with no -Q, so all five tasks routed to the `render` queue have no consumer; staging pins STORAGE_BACKEND=local, which 409s the entire presigned-multipart upload path; and test_staging_prod_compose_parity asserts only two image strings, the staging image parametrization, and pgbouncer-not-in-prod. (E3) send_notification writes NotificationDelivery(status=sent) BEFORE dispatch and NOTIFY_BACKEND defaults to "console" (a logger.info) with the value set in no deploy artifact, so the DB records `sent` for every transactional email while nothing leaves the box — and the UNIQUE dedupe_key latch then permanently blocks a re-send if the backend is later fixed. Plus (E7) two tests headed "price-book math" that compute minutes*COST_PER_MIN_DEEPGRAM in the test body and assert it equals a hand-computed constant, over a production code path that does not exist — transcription, embedding, R2 and render CPU cost are recorded nowhere, and PRICE_BOOK_VERSION is a rate-change sentinel stored and compared by nothing. Also: R2 bucket CORS set from sys.argv and reconciled with ALLOWED_ORIGINS by nothing; OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI validated for scheme only, never for whether its path resolves in app.routes; CSRF_FETCH_METADATA_ENABLED off by default, set by no deploy artifact, with a green test asserting cross-site POST succeeds; doctor.py covering 22 of 214 settings via a literal _SECTIONS list, and tests/test_backup_config.py:37 structurally forbidding any production-boot signal about backups. Checked and found clean (so nobody re-derives): all four flags.py kill switches are genuinely enforced; the "unreferenced" sentry_environment/logs_database_url are consumed via @property; .dockerignore correctly excludes .env; the existing prod validators in config.py are correct — the gap is coverage, not correctness. candidates.title: run_layer0.py: ruff/mypy/bandit/pip-audit report a PERFECT SCORE when the tool exits non-zero, and --require cannot see it
candidates.evidence: .claude/skills/production-assessment/scripts/run_layer0.py:159-164 (ruff), :170-172 (mypy), :227-231 (bandit), :274-281 (pip-audit); --require semantics at :589-592
candidates.claims_to_verify: That the required check 'Types + SAST + deps (mypy, bandit, pip-audit)' proves ruff=0 issues, mypy=0 errors, bandit=0 HIGH/0 MEDIUM and pip-audit=0 vulnerabilities against the strict baselines.json floor of 0.
candidates.why_hollow: None of the four inspects proc.returncode; each infers the result purely from stdout and treats EMPTY stdout as a clean result (`json.loads(proc.stdout or "[]")`, `or "{}"`, and for mypy a bare count of ': error:' lines with no unparseable branch at all). A tool that runs and fails writes diagnostics to stderr and leaves stdout empty -> the gate returns {'status':'ok','value':0}, the best possible score, which passes a baseline of 0. This is strictly worse than the documented 'skipped' path because main() implements --require as 'fail if status == skipped'; a gate whose status is 'ok' is invisible to it. Adding --require ruff,mypy,bandit,pip_audit to static-gates -- the fix the process map recommends -- would not help. Verified against the real binaries: invalid [tool.ruff] key -> rc=2/0 bytes stdout; _sources() empty -> mypy rc=2/0 bytes; pip-audit with OSV/PyPI unreachable or a bad -r -> rc=1/0 bytes stdout, gate reports '0 vulnerabilities' on a REQUIRED check.
candidates.repro:
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, pathlib, sys
p = pathlib.Path(".claude/skills/production-assessment/scripts/run_layer0.py")
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("l0", p); m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
m._CANDIDATE_SOURCES = []          # _sources() -> []  => mypy invoked with zero targets
sys.argv = ["run_layer0.py", "--gates", "mypy", "--require", "mypy"]
print("EXIT CODE (even WITH --require mypy):", m.main())
PY
=> prints 'mypy  ok  0' then 'All runnable gates passed.' EXIT CODE: 0, while the underlying mypy process exits 2 with 'mypy: error: Missing target module, package, files, or command.'
candidates.modality: A — CI gates and exit-code plumbing
candidates.verifier: run_layer0.py infers each static gate's result purely from stdout and never inspects `proc.returncode`, so a tool that runs and FAILS (diagnostics on stderr, empty stdout) is scored as a perfect result — `{'status':'ok','value':0}` — which passes the strict baselines.json floor of 0. Reproduced against the real .venv binaries: mypy with zero targets or a bad --config-file exits 2 with 0 bytes stdout; ruff with a malformed --config exits 2 with 0 bytes; pip-audit with the network unreachable or a bad -r exits 1 with 0 bytes. `--require` cannot catch any of it, because it only escalates a 'skipped' status and these report 'ok' (verified end-to-end: `--gates mypy --require mypy` prints "mypy ok 0 / All runnable gates passed" and returns exit 0 while mypy exited 2 having checked nothing). Two corrections to the candidate: (1) SCOPE — ruff is independently guarded by the separate required CI job `lint` (ci.yml:58-70, bare `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .`) and by scripts/ci_local.sh:69-75, so only mypy, bandit and pip-audit are genuinely unguarded; the practical CI blast radius is the `static-gates` required check silently green-lighting a type/SAST/dependency scan that never produced a verdict, most plausibly pip-audit reporting "0 vulnerabilities" during a PyPI/OSV outage. (2) MECHANISM — bandit's realistic failure (missing target dir) exits 0 and emits JSON with a populated `"errors"` array and empty `"results"`, so bandit is hollow via the ignored `errors` list rather than the ignored returncode; its empty-stdout path requires a config-load failure. Severity medium, not high: a gate hole with no live exposure, requiring a co-occurring tool failure, on a ≤100-user beta. Fix must check `proc.returncode` (and bandit's `errors[]`) and return 'skipped'/'fail' rather than a 0 — and `static-gates` should also pass `--require ruff,mypy,bandit,pip_audit`, which is necessary but, as shown, not sufficient on its own.

candidates.modality: A — CI gates and exit-code plumbing
candidates.verifier:
The production deploy preflight (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml:279`) runs `python scripts/doctor.py` without `--full`, so the deploy gate live-probes only Postgres and Redis. The `Live — external APIs` section — including the `_live_stripe` and `_live_r2` probes that were deliberately hardened on 2026-08-13 to drive the app's OWN clients (`billing.stripe_client._STRIPE`, `worker.storage._r2`) after those probes' bypass hid a 10-week Stripe outage — is appended only under `if full:` (`scripts/doctor.py:454-474`). A repo-wide caller census shows `--full` appears exclusively in human runbooks (SECRETS.md, ACCESS.md, runbooks/24-25-26, GO_LIVE); `deploy.yml` and `scripts/deploy.sh:97` are the only automated callers and neither passes it. `tests/test_doctor.py:6` states the live checks are "exercised manually via --full". The fix made in response to the outage therefore has no automated caller.

Scope corrections to the original candidate:
- It is NOT true that the preflight "probes no external dependency at all": Postgres and Redis are genuinely live-probed.
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` never mentions doctor.py (0 hits in 495 lines); the "live-probes all seven" description comes from `docs/SOT.md:298`, `docs/DECISIONS.md:10471-10474` and this audit's own process-map.
- R2 is NOT unguarded: `_section_storage` hard-FAILs on missing R2_* whenever `STORAGE_BACKEND=r2` (which deploy.yml:247-253 pins), and the post-rollout smoke hard-gates on `/health` returning `status=="ok"`, which requires `_check_storage()` -> `worker.storage._r2().head_bucket` to succeed through the app's own client, with auto-rollback on failure. The unset R2_* GitHub secrets make the sync a no-op but do not create an unverified path.
- The `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY -> WARN, exit 0` hole is closed by `config.py:1129-1141`, which raises in `ENV=production` when the Stripe secrets are unset, so the app fails to boot and the smoke rolls back.
- The preflight is also not the only gate: a full staging-gate job (migrate + `llm_harness --flow core` against a data-bearing DB) runs before the prod job.

Residual, accurate risk: the app's Voyage, Deepgram and Stripe client paths are verified by nothing automated at any point in the deploy — only by presence/format checks against `.env` strings. Anthropic has partial coverage via the nightly `llm-e2e-nightly.yml` against the same GitHub secret that is synced to the VM. Fix is one flag (`--full`) plus a decision on whether third-party flakiness should be allowed to block a deploy; if it should not, split the external probes into a non-blocking post-deploy step so a red Stripe/Voyage/Deepgram probe is at least visible.

Adjacent (separate finding, not part of A4): `CC_JWT_SECRET` is not set in GitHub secrets, so deploy.yml:368-370's Phase-2 critical-journey smoke prints "WARNING: CC_JWT_SECRET not set — skipping critical journey smoke" and is skipped on every production deploy, leaving `/health` as the sole post-rollout gate.

candidates.title: gate_module_coverage reports 'ok' when the floor-gated modules are absent from coverage.xml, defeating the Issue-479 --require hardening
candidates.evidence: .claude/skills/production-assessment/scripts/run_layer0.py:396-413 (`if rate is None: ... continue`), :481 (_evaluate reads only _failures); guard test tests/test_layer0_module_coverage.py:86-95; caller .github/workflows/ci.yml:250-253
candidates.claims_to_verify: Per-module coverage floors on five load-bearing modules (clip_engine 91.0, preference 88.0, crypto 99.0, limiter 99.0, auth 99.0), made hard by `--require coverage,module_coverage,diff_cover` so that 'a skip of ANY of them is a hard job failure, never a green no-op' (ci.yml comment).
candidates.why_hollow: The gate has two ways to enforce nothing and --require covers only one. Missing/unparseable coverage.xml -> status 'skipped' -> --require fires (that is Issue 479, fixed). But if coverage.xml EXISTS and simply lacks the module, _module_line_rate returns None, the loop `continue`s, _failures stays empty, and _evaluate sets status 'ok' -- which --require is satisfied by. All five floors can read 'unknown' and the required job goes green. This is literally the Issue-368 failure (run_layer0.py:325-331: 'these two sat at 0.0 -- i.e. unenforceable -- because the multi-root --cov flattened their files into package "." and _module_line_rate returned None. They were never low-coverage; they were unmeasured.'). Issue 368 fixed the cause and left the silent-continue in place. Worse, the anti-hollowing test guards the wrong half: test_every_floored_module_is_resolvable_in_principle is documented as 'no module may sit at an unenforceable 0.0' but only asserts the floors dict is non-empty and no floor VALUE is <= 0.0 -- it never touches a coverage report. Nothing asserts the five modules actually resolve in the real _coverage.xml.
candidates.repro:
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
